question: Related Questions Q. Share of wife in husband's property which is purchased by his own earnings 2276 views Q. Can a Muslim gift his self earned property after disowning his surviving son to his grandsons and wife and three daughters? 4032 views Q. Why is a daughter given only 1/3rd share of her fathers property after her fathers death. Why she is not given equal share. Please elaborate the answer. 3124 views Q. Am I obligated to give a share of my property to my son who married our former maid, despite my concerns about his wife's intentions? 1756 views Q. Inheritance 1633 views Q. 11th October 2010 / 2nd Zul Qadah 1431 Assalamou alaikum Respected Mufti sahib, I live in England, United Kingdom. I am a widow, my husband passed away nearly 3 months ago. I have 9 sons and 2 daughters. My husband?s mother is also alive. My late husband was the owner of two houses. Some months prior to his death, my husband made me a joint owner in one of these properties. Upon the instructions of my late husband, a solicitor completed the legal paperwork and we both signed various documents in the presence of witnesses. After the death of my husband, my children requested a scholar to explain the rules of Islamic inheritance so we could distribute my husband?s wealth according to the Shariah. When the discussion arose about the joint ownership of one of the houses, the scholar was of the opinion that this transfer of joint ownership was not valid because it seemed to him that this was only done symbolically and not as a genuine gift. However, beside the legal paperwork there is no other document available to support or negate the intention of the deceased. The scholar also said that even if the above gift was genuine, this kind of gift is faasid because of the following rule of Hiba: ومن وهب شقصاً مشاعاً فالهبة فاسدةٌ، فإن قسمه وسلمه جاز ) الهداية شرح بداية المبتدي,ص225,ج3, الناشر المكتبة الإسلامية) Which in essence says, if the item is such that if it is divided it can still be of use, then it is not permissible to give it without dividing it. Such items are ?a plot of land, a big house...?. See Bahishti Zewar (link below) page 66 point 5 http://www.islamicbulletin.org/free_downloads/women/bahishti_4_5_6_7.pdf I would be grateful if you would clarify (a) whether a house in the UK falls within the category of divisible property; (b) whether according to the Shariah I am the rightful owner of 50% of the house which was in joint ownership between myself and my husband. answer: Transactions & Dealings >> Inheritance & Will Question ID: 29897 Country: India Title: What do the Scholars say about the following question? My grandfather, Late Saeed Hasan, passed away 60 years ago. At the time of his death, his wife i.e. my grandmother and his 2 sons, Hafiz Syed Qasier Naseem and Syed Shariful Hasan were present. After that, my grandmother passed away in 1985. At the time of her death, his two sons Hafiz Syed Qaiser Naseem and Syed Shariful Hasan were present. Then my father, Hafiz Syed Qaiser Naseem passed away in 1993. Kindly let me know in the light of Quran and Sunnah how the total property and assets will be distributed among the two sons of my grandfather, Late Saeed Hasan. I will be very thankful to you Eagerly waiting for your reply Seeking your good cooperation Question: What do the Scholars say about the following question? My grandfather, Late Saeed Hasan, passed away 60 years ago. At the time of his death, his wife i.e. my grandmother and his 2 sons, Hafiz Syed Qasier Naseem and Syed Shariful Hasan were present. After that, my grandmother passed away in 1985. At the time of her death, his two sons Hafiz Syed Qaiser Naseem and Syed Shariful Hasan were present. Then my father, Hafiz Syed Qaiser Naseem passed away in 1993. Kindly let me know in the light of Quran and Sunnah how the total property and assets will be distributed among the two sons of my grandfather, Late Saeed Hasan. I will be very thankful to you Eagerly waiting for your reply Seeking your good cooperation Thanks Syed Mohsin Naseem S/o Late Hafiz Syed Qaiser Naseem Address: L-27, Abul Fazl Enclave Jamia Nagar, OKhla New Delhi ? 110 025 Mob: 91 9716928632 Answer ID: 29897 Posted on: Aug 30, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 416/209/D=1432) If no one from the parents of your grandfather and grandmother was alive at the time of their death, their inheritance shall be divided into 2 shares and both their sons shall get 1-1 share. Detail: Son: 2x1 02 Total: 2 Shares Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
